show.title: A Christmas Carol: The Musical *12th Annual*
show.author: Lynn Ahrens & Mike Ockrent
show.description:
Ebenezer Scrooge is a prosperous curmudgeon who believes personal wealth is far more valuable than the happiness and comfort of others. With an infuriated "Bah! Humbug!" Scrooge summates his feelings about Christmas tidings and charitable giving, but he's forced to face his selfish ways when three ghosts on Christmas Eve lead him through his Past, Present, & Future. Thanks to their guidance, Scrooge recognizes his faults and greets Christmas morning with a cheerful "Happy Christmas" before spending the day reconnecting and sharing love with those who mean the most to him.

This is a spectacular adaptation of Charles Dickens' most well-known story that had a decade-long run at the Theatre at Madison Square Garden. The show has featured well-known actors such as Terrence Mann, Roddy McDowall, Frank Langella, Tim Curry, Roger Daltrey, Emily Skinner, Christopher Sieber, Didi Conn, Ben Vereen, and more. It was made into a movie starring Kelsey Grammer, Jesse L. Martin, Jane Krakowski, Jennifer Love Hewitt, and Jason Alexander. You will love it!

Runtime is approximately 90 minutes. No intermission.

Contains some mild adult language.

Character Descriptions
The following roles are available:

Ebeneezer Scrooge - Vocal range A3-G5. An old man whose great wealth has turned his heart to stone. Deaf to the needs of his fellow men. Scrooge must journey through his life to regain the spirit of charity and kindness he had as a young man. He transforms from miserly to merry. Must be able to show a full range of emotions – angry, fearful, wistful, sad, boyishly delighted.

Ghost of Christmas Present/Sandwich Board Man - Vocal range A3-G5. A jolly showman who shows Scrooge the truths of the present, both the good and the bad. Vaudeville!  Should move well. Tap experience a plus, but not required.

Ghost of Christmas Future/Blind Old Hag - Vocal range C4-F5. Needs to be able to belt and have a strong mix. Strong and mostly silent as she shows Scrooge what will happen to him and those around him if he continues down the path he is currently treading. Creepy and eerie, yet captivating every time they are on stage. Potentially split into 2 roles. (Prepare contemporary combination)

Tiny Tim - Vocal range B-flat 3-D5. Mr. and Mrs. Cratchit's youngest son. He is crippled and sick but is the definition of loving Christmas spirit. He constantly reminds his family that they will be happy as long as they have each other. Represents the Christmas spirit with hope and goodness.

Fred Anderson - Vocal range A2-F4. Scrooge's nephew and only living relative. He believes in the good a joyful Christmas spirit can make in the world. Warm and compassionate, Scrooge's nephew feels sorry for the old man, yet feels familial obligation to him. He is essentially who Scrooge was before Marley died.

Scrooge at 18 - Vocal range B2-G4. Scrooge with the happiness of his youth and deeply in love with Emily. Sincere and warm until grasped by greed.

Emily - Vocal range B3-B-flat 5. Scrooge's fiancé from when they were young. She is a beautiful girl, not impressed by or in need of money. Enjoys the simple things in life. Joyful and kind-hearted. In love with Scrooge at 18.

Mr. Fezziwig -  Vocal range B2-B4. Must be able to move. A jolly and kind man who used to throw a huge Christmas party every year for the community. He was Scrooge's first boss and after teaching him all he knew, he became deeply disappointed in the man Scrooge became.

Mrs. Fezziwig - Vocal range A3-A-flat 5. Must be able to move. The consummate hostess and Mr. Fezziwig's wife, she loved to help throw the Christmas party every year. Fun and sassy.

Sally Anderson - Vocal range C4-E-flat 5. Wife of Fred. Warm and loving.

Jonathan - Vocal range E-flat 4-E-flat 5. Fun street urchin. Comedic.

Mr. Smythe - Vocal range D-flat 3-F-sharp 4. Recently widowed. Hopeful. Poor and in debt to Scrooge. Father of Grace.

Beadle - Vocal range A2-B-flat 3. Worker in the royal exchange.

Old Joe - Vocal range F3-C-sharp 4. Scavenger of the dead.

Young Marley - Vocal range D3-F-sharp 4. Must be able to move. Starts business with Scrooge at 18 and shares a similar mindset of greed.

Scrooge at 12 - Vocal range F-sharp 3-A4. Poor orphan Scrooge works in a factory and vows to save his money. Misses and loves his sister, Fan.

Grace Smythe - Vocal range D-flat 4-F-sharp 5. Daughter of Mr. Smythe. Sad yet hopeful.

Fan at 10 - Vocal range A4-E5. Younger sister to Scrooge. Must be able to dance (prepare contemporary combination).

Martha Cratchit - Sister to Tiny Tim. Loves her family.

Scrooge's Mother - Vocal range C4-C5. Sad yet beautiful cameo moment.

Acolytes - 4 featured dancers (prepare contemporary combination)

Christmas Cracker Dancers - 2 featured dancers (prepare contemporary combination)

show.title: Lost in Yonkers
show.author: Neil Simon
show.description: Neil Simon’s Pulitzer Prize–winning Lost in Yonkers is a richly funny, deeply human comedy about family, survival, and growing up when you’re least prepared to do so. When two young brothers are sent to live with their formidable grandmother, they’re plunged into a household full of unforgettable characters: a childlike aunt, a sharp-tongued matriarch, and a mysterious uncle with ties to the mob. Simon’s trademark humor crackles throughout, delivering laugh-out-loud moments alongside unexpected tenderness. Widely regarded as Simon’s most accomplished play, Lost in Yonkers balances comedy and compassion, reminding us that even the most complicated families can shape us in surprising—and often hilarious—ways.

show.title: Reefer Madness: The Musical
show.author: Kevin Murphy and Dan Studney
show.description:
Inspired by the original 1936 film of the same name, this raucous musical comedy takes a tongue-in-cheek look at the hysteria caused when clean-cut kids fall prey to marijuana, leading them on a hysterical downward spiral filled with evil jazz music, sex and violence.

You won’t be able to resist the spoofy fun of Reefer Madness. The addictive, clever musical numbers range from big Broadway-style showstoppers to swing tunes like “Down at the Ol’ Five and Dime” and the Vegas-style “Listen to Jesus, Jimmy,” featuring J.C. Himself leading a chorus of showgirl angels. Refeer Madness is a highly stylized and satirical political commentary that will leave you wanting more.

show.title: Stephen King's Misery
show.author: William Goldman (based on the novel by Stephen King)
show.description: This psychological thriller based on Stephen King's novel Misery follows successful romance novelist Paul Sheldon, who is rescued from a car crash and wakes up captive in a secluded home owned by his self-identified "number one fan," Annie Wilkes. While Paul is convalescing, Annie reads the manuscript of his latest book and becomes enraged when she discovers the author has killed off her favorite character, Misery Chastain. Annie forces Paul to write a new Misery novel and he quickly realizes Annie has no intention of letting him go. The irate Annie has Paul writing as if his life depends on it – and it does.

show.title: Dear Evan Hansen

show.description: A letter that was never meant to be seen, a lie that was never meant to be told, a life he never dreamed he could have. Evan Hansen is about to get the one thing he’s always wanted: a change to finally fit in. Dear Evan Hansen is the deeply personal and profoundly contemporary musical about life and the way we live it.

show.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
show.author: Christopher Sergel (adapted from the novel by Harper Lee)
show.description: Set in the small Southern town of Maycomb, Alabama, during the Great Depression, To Kill a Mockingbird is a powerful story about childhood, family, justice, prejudice, courage, and the loss of innocence. Seen largely through the eyes of Scout Finch, the story follows her father Atticus, a respected attorney appointed to defend Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of assaulting a white woman. As the trial divides the community, Scout and Jem discover that the adult world is far more complicated than they imagined, learning lessons about empathy, integrity, and standing for what is right even at personal cost. Running alongside the trial is the children's fascination with their mysterious neighbor, Arthur 'Boo' Radley.

show.title: Les Misérables
show.author: Alain Boublil & Claude-Michel Schönberg (based on the novel by Victor Hugo)
show.description: Among the most celebrated and longest-running musicals ever staged, Les Misérables follows Jean Valjean, a former prisoner who devotes his life to earning redemption. Set in 19th-century France in the years after the French Revolution, the story weaves together many lives and shows both the power of compassion and the quiet cruelty of ignoring human suffering. Valjean's search for a fresh start takes him to Paris and ultimately to the barricades of the student uprising, all while Inspector Javert and the shadows of his past pursue him. In the struggle for the soul of the city, he finds what love and salvation truly mean. Staged in more than 40 countries and 22 languages, the musical brings Victor Hugo's sweeping novel to vivid life through a rich, soaring score that includes "I Dreamed a Dream," "On My Own," and "Bring Him Home." Theatre of the Republic is producing it as the opening show of its 2027 season.

show.title: Charlotte's Web
show.author: Joseph Robinette (adapted from the novel by E.B. White)
show.description: When Wilbur, a small pig with a big heart, learns that his future on the farm is uncertain, he finds an unexpected champion in Charlotte — a wise and wonderful spider with a talent for writing. With the help of Fern, who understands the language of animals, and Templeton, a reluctant but resourceful rat, Charlotte hatches a plan to change Wilbur's fate. As mysterious messages begin appearing in her web, the barnyard — and soon the whole town — takes notice. Gentle, funny, and deeply moving, Charlotte's Web is a classic, heartwarming tale that celebrates loyalty, kindness, and what it truly means to be a friend.

show.title: Come From Away
show.author: Irene Sankoff & David Hein
show.description: Come From Away tells the remarkable true story of a small town that welcomed the world. On September 11, 2001, 38 planes carrying nearly 7,000 passengers were unexpectedly grounded in Gander, Newfoundland, nearly doubling the town's population overnight. As fear and uncertainty gripped the world, the people of Gander opened their homes, hearts, and community to stranded travelers from across the globe. Filled with soaring music, humor, and humanity, this critically acclaimed musical celebrates the power of community and the extraordinary kindness that can emerge in the face of tragedy.

show.author: Frederick Knott (adapted by Jeffrey Hatcher)
show.description: Tony Award-winning suspense thriller set in Greenwich Village in 1944. Susan Hendrix, who is blind but resourceful, is targeted by a band of ruthless criminals hunting for a mysterious doll stuffed with contraband. As the danger escalates, Susan has to rely on her wits and her nerve to outsmart her attackers in a tense battle of cunning, building to a breathtaking final scene. Directed by Dalton Isaac; stage managed by Michelle Wagoner. The production will be staged in the round, with the audience on all sides.

show.title: Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow Moscow
show.author: Halley Feiffer
show.description: A contemporary comic twist on Chekhov's Three Sisters. Since their brother Andrey gambled away the family fortune, Olga, Masha and Irina have been stuck in the dull Russian countryside, longing to return to Moscow and the exciting lives they feel they deserve. When the military arrives in town with variety, entertainment and plenty of chaos, Moscow suddenly seems within reach as this hilariously dysfunctional family wrestles with class, culture and love. Directed by Stuart Parks II. Theatre of Dare's 'Dinner & a Show' production, performed upstairs at The Black Pelican Restaurant.
